dataset_title: ICMR Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance Network Annual Report
issuing_authority: Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), New Delhi, India
geographic_scope: National (India - Multi-center surveillance across tertiary medical centers)
sample_size_note: sample_size_total_isolates (98400) is the figure declared in the source dataset header. per_antimicrobial_test_count_sum (166100) is the arithmetic sum of the per-row sample_size values below and is computed from this file, not quoted from the source. The two figures are not the same quantity and must not be reported interchangeably. The most likely explanation is that a single isolate is tested against multiple antimicrobials, but this relationship has NOT been verified against the ICMR source publication. Do not cite the 166100 figure as an isolate count.

antibiogram.clinical_implication: High empirical failure rate; avoid empirical fluoroquinolones for uncomplicated UTI in India per ICMR recommendations.
Remains highly susceptible (>85%); first-line Access agent for uncomplicated cystitis.
Moderate resistance; suitable as second-line or culture-guided therapy.
High ESBL prevalence; 3rd-generation cephalosporin monotherapy ineffective for serious hospital-acquired infections.
Significant carbapenem resistance (CRKP); carbapenem stewardship essential.
Over 40% MRSA rate in Indian tertiary care; consider MRSA coverage in purulent sepsis.
100% susceptibility maintained; no confirmed VRSA in network.
Highly active; reserve group agent strictly preserved for MDR Gram-positive infections.
High susceptibility maintained (>90%); confirms Amoxicillin as first-line for CAP.
High macrolide resistance; avoid macrolide monotherapy for pneumococcal pneumonia.
